https://hungarytoday.hu/industrial-outpu.text: Industrial Output Fell Short of Expectations in June Industrial production indicators for June fell short of expectations; preliminary GDP data had already suggested that the final month of the first half of the year had not been particularly strong—based on analysts’ assessments reported by MTI. According to the first estimate released Thursday by the Central Statistical Office (KSH), the volume of industrial production in June rose by 10.1 percent year-over-year and by 4.1 percent on a working-day-adjusted basis, as there were two more working days in June of this year than in the previous year. In the previous month, the working-day-adjusted annual growth in production was 5.4 percent. Compared to the previous month, seasonally and working-day-adjusted industrial production fell by 1.4 percent, after growth of 2.7 percent had been recorded in May. Industrial Production in Hungary (2002–2026, January–June): Annual Change in Production Volume Compared with the Same Period of the Previous Year. Chart: MTI The industrial production data for June came in significantly better than expected but still fell short of the market consensus, and the monthly decline in production was a disappointment, noted János Nagy, a macroeconomist at Erste Bank. He observed that considerable uncertainty continues to surround the outlook for the manufacturing sector. Although the order backlog has already risen significantly in recent months, growth has not been uniform, while the external environment continues to be characterized by subdued growth, and the stronger forint exchange rate is also hampering the industry’s international competitiveness. Foreign demand will be the decisive factor in determining how quickly the manufacturing sector can recover and at what pace the newly added production capacity will be ramped up, according to him. Major industrial subsectors, including vehicle manufacturing, electronics, and electrical equipment production, recorded year-on-year growth. Photo: MTI/Tibor Katona Péter Virovácz, chief economist at ING Bank, believes that Hungarian industry cannot break away from its usual pattern: one good month, one bad month. The somewhat disappointing GDP data for the second quarter already suggested that the monthly statistics for June would not be as strong. The KSH has not yet released many details. However, even based on the brief commentary, a generally positive picture is emerging, as production volume has increased in most sectors of the manufacturing industry. Battery production also appears to have bottomed out, as growth was recorded in this sector as well. Paks power plant. Photo: MTI/Hegedüs Róbert Looking ahead, industrial statistics are expected to be significantly impacted by the decline in production resulting from the crisis in Paks. Accordingly, substantial negative figures are expected as early as July, but especially in the August data. However, if a complete shutdown in Paks can be avoided, there is a chance that a recovery could begin as early as the fall. Despite the current crisis, the ING Bank expert believes that Hungary’s total industrial output could even grow by about 3 to 4 percent in 2026. This means that after three years of industrial recession, the sector could once again make a positive contribution to the overall performance of the Hungarian economy, despite the crisis in Paks. Gábor Regős, chief economist at the asset management firm Gránit, emphasized that the sector may already have passed its lowest point—at least for the time being. Industrial output may have contributed positively to GDP growth on both an annual and quarterly basis, but this will only become clear from the detailed GDP data. Factors playing a role here include, on the one hand, slightly improved foreign demand and, on the other hand, production capacities that were created as a result of major domestic investments and have now begun production. Photo: MTI/Kovács Márton The war in Iran will certainly be a decisive factor in shaping expectations for the coming months, as it not only leads to higher energy prices from time to time but also unsettles economic actors. Higher energy prices are undermining the competitiveness of Hungarian industry and are also dampening foreign demand. This summer, the production outage at the Paks Nuclear Power Plant and the resulting restrictions will pose an even greater problem. Dániel Molnár, senior analyst at the GFÜ Economic Analysis Center, pointed out that following the exceptional growth in May, the sector corrected itself on a monthly basis, with output declining by 1.4 percent; nevertheless, the second quarter as a whole was marked by a significant increase of 1.7 percent compared to the previous quarter. Considerable uncertainty continues to surround the outlook for the industrial sector. Although the order backlog has already risen significantly in recent months, growth has been uneven, while the external environment continues to be characterized by subdued growth and the stronger forint exchange rate is also undermining the industry’s international competitiveness. The effects of the shutdown of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant and the voluntary energy consumption restrictions are expected to be reflected in the August data; however, if the situation returns to normal shortly, no lasting negative effects are anticipated. He noted that foreign demand will therefore continue to be the decisive factor in determining how quickly the industry can recover and at what pace new production capacity will be ramped up. https://www.pressenza.com/2026/08/the-us.text: Search The US is replicating its anti-Russian regional containment model against China. Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby gave a landmark speech in Manilla during the first leg of his Southeast Asian tour in early August that amounted to the US introducing the NATO 3.0 concept to the region. As Trump 2.0’s military-strategic mastermind explained it, the US is offloading more of the responsibility for maintaining regional status quos onto its allies and partners that share the same interest, which in this context is “an Asia free from hegemony”. The unstated purpose is to contain China. He cited the National Security Strategy , the National Defense Strategy , and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth’s speech at late May’s Shangri La Dialogue to justify Trump 2.0’s policy of “maintaining a posture of deterrence by denial along the first island chain” from Japan to Borneo. The Philippines sits in the middle and is therefore irreplaceable to building what’s been described elsewhere as AUKUS+. Readers can learn more about this concept and its US-backed Japanese-Philippine(- Indonesian ?) core here . In his words, “we are actively building a strong denial defense to back up a peace through strength approach of a lastingly favorable balance of power in Asia. We are systematically strengthening our forward posture, hardening our footprint, and driving deep interoperability with key countries that are willing to shoulder their share of the burden. This is not merely about performing in symbolic exercises for the cameras; it is about fielding combat-credible forces capable of defeating real military aggression.” This leaves no doubt about the US’ intent to contain China by “ Leading From Behind ” in the Asia-Pacific upon the region’s implementation of the NATO 3.0 concept through the accelerated construction of the AUKUS+ network. Of importance, Colby pointed out that the Philippines is “a model ally”, which is what Hegseth described Poland as while there during the first leg of his European tour in early 2025. It can therefore be assumed that the US envisages it playing a similar role in the region. Accordingly, observers should expect that the Philippines will become the US’ regional military bastion primed to play the leading role in containing China by dint of its geostrategic location just like Poland vis-à-vis Russia as recently confirmed by President Karol Nawrocki, all in close coordination with the US. Of course, the Philippines can’t do this on its own just like Poland can’t either, but their respective roles in containing the US’ regional adversaries are mostly as logistical bases and launchpads for US forces. In practice, the end goal is for them to host enough supplies, US forces, and missiles to correspondingly deter China from making a military move on Taiwan and Russia from doing the same on Ukraine after the ongoing hostilities finally end, otherwise the Philippines and Poland will intervene then the US will follow. Japan is being primed for the same role as the Philippines but might not involve itself in hostilities at first for escalation-control reasons and to avoid a global economic shock if China directly retaliates. Its economy is much more important to the world’s than Poland’s, let alone the Philippines, but all three are the US’ mutual defense allies so any direct retaliation by China or Russia instead of only attacking their forces in Taiwan and Ukraine respectively in each scenario would prompt an American response. As can be discerned from Colby’s speech, the US is replicating its anti-Russian regional containment model against China, which has enormous implications for global stability and raises the risk of World War III. Shaheen’s daughter, Stefany Shaheen, is among those seeking the Democratic nomination for Pappas’ seat, along with former candidate Maura Sullivan. Europe Former World Chess Champion Kasparov Says US Warned Him About Kremlin Kill Plot Garry Kasparov, a critic of the Kremlin, said he would not hide and added, ‘My family and I will not truly be safe as long as Putin is in power in Russia.’ Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print Former world chess champion Garry Kasparov at his office in Manhattan, New York City, on June 13, 2016. Benjamin Chasteen/The Epoch Times Chris Summers 10/2/2026 | Updated: 10/2/2026 0:00 X 1 Former world chess ‌champion Garry Kasparov has said the security services from both the United States and ‌Lithuania have warned him that his ⁠life was in danger, after a Russian plot was discovered which allegedly targeted Kremlin critics living abroad. Last month the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) said five people had been charged with plotting, on behalf of Russian intelligence, to ⁠assassinate two opposition figures. One of the targets was in the United States, and the other in Lithuania. DOJ did not identify Kasparov—who moved to the United States from Russia in 2013 and lives in New York—but in a Substack post the 63-year-old former chess grandmaster said he had been warned his life was in danger. He identified the other person as Ivan Tyutrin, the co-founder of the Free Russia Forum, who is based in Lithuania. “Neither I nor Ivan have been told explicitly that we were the targets whose names are redacted in the indictment of the assassins,” Kasparov said. Related Stories House, Senate Vote to Give Russian Dissident Vladimir Kara-Murza Honorary Citizenship Top NATO Commander Says China, Russia, Iran, North Korea Increasingly Cooperating “We were, however, warned by security services in Lithuania and the United States that our lives were in danger and that we should take precautions, which I did and will continue to do.” The Epoch Times reached out to the Free Russia Forum for comment, but did not receive a response by publication time. Kasparov—who was born in Baku in what is now Azerbaijan, when it was part of the Soviet Union—became famous when, at the age of 22, he beat Anatoly Karpov to become world chess champion, a title he held until 2000. Russian riot policemen detain former world chess champion Garry Kasparov outside a court building in Moscow on Aug. 17, 2012. Andrey Smirnov/AFP/GettyImages Kasparov, an increasingly outspoken critic of Russian President Vladimir Putin, chairs the Renew Democracy Initiative, a nonprofit that describes itself as an “intellectual home for the pro-democracy movement” globally. In his The Next Move Substack, Kasparov said his friend and fellow opposition figure, Boris Nemtsov, was “murdered in cold blood in front of the Kremlin” in February 2015. ‘I Will Not Hide’: Kasparov “But I will not stop, and I will not hide, even if I thought it was possible to do so. I believe that the best defense is a good offense,” Kasparov said. “My family and I will not truly be safe as long as Putin is in power in Russia—a circumstance shared by millions.” The DOJ only referred to the targets of the alleged Russian intelligence plot as Victim-1, who lived in the United States, and Victim-2, who lived in Lithuania. They said a U.S. national had been offered $40,000 to “eliminate” or “disappear” Victim-1. A U.S. citizen was also contacted about surveilling and murdering Victim-2, who was allegedly described by the plotters as a “bad guy” who was “telling lies about Russia.” The Kremlin said last month it saw no reason to comment on the U.S. allegations, saying there was an absence of credible evidence and facts. Russia has ⁠previously denied conducting such plots on foreign soil. Reuters contributed to this report.
